title: Folders inside folders
objectives: Find any file in a folder tree by following one route down from the top
Name the parent of a file or folder
Write and read a path from the top of a tree

screens.prose: This is everything in Ana's home folder, `ana`. Each pill is a folder or a file. A line joins a folder to each thing directly inside it.
screens.question: Tap the folder that directly holds `backtest.py`.

hints.text: Find `backtest.py` first, then follow its line one step back towards `ana`.
Here is the file.
The line from `backtest.py` leads back to `src`. Tap `src`.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start at the file and step back along one line only.

byKey.a-p: `project` holds `src`, and `src` holds the file. You went two steps back instead of one.
byKey.a: `ana` holds everything here, but only through other folders. Step back one line from the file.
byKey.a-p-s-bt: That is the file itself. Tap the folder it sits in.

explain.text: You stepped back one line from `backtest.py` and reached `src`. Every file sits in exactly one folder. Folders can sit inside folders, which is why the picture branches like a tree.

screens.prose: To open a file you start at the top and open one folder at a time. Tap your way down from `ana` to `ideas.md`.
screens.question: Tap every pill on the way from `ana` to `ideas.md`, both ends included.

hints.text: Which folder inside `ana` leads towards `notes`?
The route runs through `project`.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Follow the lines, and tap each pill you pass.

byKey.skip-project: You jumped from `ana` straight to `notes`. No line joins them: `notes` sits inside `project`.
byKey.only-ends: You tapped the two ends. Tap the folders in between too.
byKey.a-dl: `Downloads` is a side branch. The route to `ideas.md` never enters it.
byKey.a-p-s: `src` is a side branch. The route to `ideas.md` goes through `notes`.

explain.text: You opened `ana`, then `project`, then `notes`, and found `ideas.md`. There was only one route. Every item in a tree has exactly one route down from the top.

screens.prose: The folder directly above an item is its **parent**. On the first screen you found the parent of `backtest.py`: `src`. Folders have parents too.
screens.question: Tap the parent of the folder `data`.

hints.text: Step back one line from `data`, towards the top.
Here is `data`.
One line back from `data` is `project`.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The parent is one line above, never more.

byKey.a: `ana` is two lines above `data`. It is the parent of `project`, the folder above `data`.
byKey.a-p-d-pr: `prices.csv` sits inside `data`, so it is below it. A parent is always above.
byKey.a-p-d: That is `data` itself. Tap the folder it sits in.

explain.text: You went one line up from `data` and reached `project`. Every item except the top one has exactly one parent. A file can never be a parent, because nothing sits inside a file.

screens.prose: Writing the route down saves Ana from describing it. We list the folders from the top, joined by `/`, and end with the file. That written route is the file's **path**.
screens.question: Build the path to the highlighted `prices.csv`, starting from `ana`.

hints.text: Read the highlighted route from left to right.
The route passes through these folders.
The route is `ana`, `project`, `data`, `prices.csv`, with a `/` between each pair.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. List the pills along the highlighted route, top first, with `/` between them.

byKey.dl: `Downloads` holds a different `prices.csv`. The highlighted one is inside `project`.
byKey.src: `src` holds code. The highlighted file is inside `data`.
byKey.file: You put the file name early. The file comes last, after every folder above it.
byKey.data: Check the order. The path starts at the top, so `data` comes after `project`.

explain.text: You wrote `ana/project/data/prices.csv`. Each `/` means: open this folder, then look inside it. Read left to right, a path is the route down the tree.

screens.prose: A colleague emails Ana four paths. Only one of them leads to a real file in her tree.
screens.question: Which path leads to a file that exists?

options.why: You skipped `project`. There is no `src` directly inside `ana`.
You looked in `notes`. It holds only `ideas.md`.
You wrote the route bottom up. A path starts at the top and ends with the file.

hints.text: Follow each path from `ana`, one name at a time.
`backtest.py` is here.
From `ana` open `project`, then `src`. The file is inside.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check each step of each path against the lines in the tree.

explain.text: You followed each path from `ana` and checked every step against a line. A path is an exact address. One missing or wrong folder and it leads nowhere.

screens.prose: Two pills read `prices.csv`. Ana opens `ana/Downloads/prices.csv` and deletes half of its rows.
screens.question: What happens to `ana/project/data/prices.csv`?

options.text: Nothing. It is a different file.
It loses the same rows, because it has the same name.
options.why: You matched the files by name. They sit in different folders, so they are two separate files.

options.text: It is deleted, because two files cannot share a name.
options.why: Two files can share a name when their folders differ. Only one folder cannot hold two of the same name.

hints.text: Write out the path of each `prices.csv`.
These are the two files.
One path runs through `Downloads`, the other through `project` and `data`. Different paths mean different files.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the two paths, not the two names.

byKey.both: You treated the name as the file. The path is what picks out one file.

explain.text: The two files have the same name but different paths. Changing one leaves the other alone. A name alone is not enough to find a file; the full path is.

screens.prose: Ana makes a **shortcut** to `backtest.py` on her Desktop to open it quickly. The shortcut stores the file's path, nothing more. Later she deletes the shortcut.
screens.question: What happens to `ana/project/src/backtest.py`?

options.text: It stays where it is, unchanged.
It is deleted along with the shortcut.
options.why: You treated the shortcut as the file. It only holds the path, so deleting it removes the path note.

options.text: It moves to the Desktop in place of the shortcut.
options.why: Deleting never moves anything. The file stays in `src`, its only parent.

hints.text: What does the shortcut actually contain?
The dashed arrow is all the shortcut is.
The shortcut holds the path `ana/project/src/backtest.py`. Deleting it deletes that note, not the file.

feedback.correct: The file is untouched. Only the pointer to it is gone.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about what the shortcut holds.

byKey.deleted: You treated the shortcut as the file itself. It is a note of the path, so the file stays in `src`.

explain.text: You deleted a note that pointed at the file. The file still sits in `src`, with the same path. The reverse is the danger: delete the file and the shortcut points at nothing.

screens.prose: Every path you wrote had the same shape. Folders from the top down, then the item, with `/` between each pair: $$\text{top}\,/\,\text{folder}\,/\,\cdots\,/\,\text{parent}\,/\,\text{name}$$ The name just before the item is always its parent.
screens.question: In `ana/project/notes/ideas.md`, which part is the parent of `ideas.md`?

options.why: You took the first name. That is the top of the route, not the parent.
`project` is two steps up. It is the parent of `notes`.
That is the item itself. Its parent is the name just before it.

hints.text: Which name sits just before `ideas.md`?
Read the path backwards one step: before `ideas.md` comes `notes`.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The parent is the name just before the item.

explain.text: You read one step back from the end of the path. That is the same as stepping one line up the tree. A path and a route down the tree are the same thing written two ways.

screens.prose: Ana starts a backtest of a moving-average signal. Her project uses the layout the rest of this course uses: `data` for inputs, `src` for code, `results` for what the code produces, `notes` for writing.
screens.question: Put each file into the folder it belongs in.

hints.text: For each file, ask: did Ana download it, write it by hand, or did her code produce it?
Raw inputs go here, and nothing else.
Downloaded prices go in `data`. The script goes in `src`. The trade list and the chart are outputs, so `results`. The write-up goes in `notes`.

feedback.correct: Inputs, code, outputs and writing each have their own folder.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Sort by where each file came from: downloaded, written by hand, or produced by the code.

byKey.trades: `trades.csv` is a CSV, but the backtest wrote it. Outputs go in `results`, so raw `data` stays untouched.
byKey.png: The chart is drawn by the code. It belongs with the other outputs in `results`.
byKey.px: `spx-daily.csv` is the downloaded input. Raw inputs live in `data`.
byKey.note: `findings.md` is Ana's write-up. Writing goes in `notes`.

explain.text: You sorted by origin, not by file type: `trades.csv` and `spx-daily.csv` are both CSVs but live apart. Ana can now delete `results` and rerun the code without risking her data. Her path to the prices is `project/data/spx-daily.csv`.

ideas: Folders hold files and other folders, so a computer's storage branches like a tree.
Every item has one parent, the folder directly above it, and one route down from the top.
A path writes that route as names joined by `/`, ending with the item. Same name, different path: different file.

formula.name: A path
formula.note: Read left to right: open each folder in turn, then find the item.

summary.trap: Deleting a shortcut deletes only the shortcut. The file it pointed to stays where it was.

quiz.question: Which folder is the parent of `backtest.py`?

options.why: You took the first name in the path. That is the top, not the parent.
`project` holds `src`. It is two steps above the file.

feedback.correct: `src` comes just before the file name.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The parent is the name just before the file.

explain.text: The name just before the file is the folder that holds it. Here that is `src`.

quiz.prose: In Ana's tree, `notes` sits inside `project`, which sits inside `ana`. `notes` holds `ideas.md`.
quiz.question: Which path is written correctly?

options.why: You wrote the route from the bottom up. A path starts at the top.
You left out `project`. `notes` is not directly inside `ana`.

feedback.correct: Top first, file last, every folder in between.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. List every folder from the top, then the file.

explain.text: A path names each folder on the route from the top, in order, then the item. Missing one folder breaks it.

quiz.prose: Ana has a Desktop shortcut to `ana/project/data/prices.csv`. She deletes `prices.csv` itself from `data`, then double-clicks the shortcut.
quiz.question: What happens?

options.text: Nothing opens: the shortcut points to a path where no file now exists.
The prices open, because the shortcut kept a copy.
options.why: You treated the shortcut as a copy of the file. It holds only the path.

options.text: The deleted file comes back to `data`.
options.why: Opening a shortcut only follows its path. It cannot restore anything.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. A shortcut holds a path, not the file.

explain.text: A shortcut is a note of a path. Delete the file and the note points at nothing. Delete the shortcut and the file is untouched.
